newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent jumps over $24 hurdle on gas oil, charts.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent jumps over $24 hurdle on gas oil, charts.

text.p: IPE November Brent jumped over the $24 a barrel hurdle at midsession on Monday on bullish technicals and a resurgence in gas oil futures after below normal temperatures in the northeast U.S. over the weekend, traders said.
After closing near contract highs on Friday, Nov Brent gained momentum today after closing a gap on the continuation chart at $24 and rising to a session high of $24.11.
It slipped back to $24.08 by 1126 GMT, still up 23 cents from Friday, and analysts said Brent was knocking on the door of the next target at the post-Gulf War high of $24.39.
"I think it's just a bit of follow-through from last week with a reasonably strong close and it's just feeding off of that," said Leslie Nicholas, energy analyst at GNI Ltd.
"I don't think it's anything substantial other than technicals and the U.S. weather," he said, adding that on an intraday basis the technicals showed prices may soon stall.
"The only thing bearish in the market is that it's full of bulls," said one trader.
But October gas oil was up $4.50 at $250.00 a tonne to match the 5-1/2 year high reached on Friday.
November shot up to $242.75, gaining $7.25, as traders rolled long positions before the spot contract expires on Wednesday.
Weather Services Corp said temperatures in the northeast U.S., the world's largest heating oil market, were up to 14 degrees Fahrenheit (seven Celsius) below normal this past weekend.
But WSC said energy demand was expected to to drop until Thursday as more seasonable temperatures move into the area.
Nicholas put Brent's resistance at $24.15 and then $24.27 to $24.39 where previous highs exist on the continuation chart.
